messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected for streaming generation in us-west-2 — SLO breach threshold crossed. auto-page -> sam (oncall). routing subsystem flagged high error-rate on router shard group r-14.

sam (oncall): I'm on it, joining bridge. observed customer-facing streaming stalls for ~3m. any correlation with recent routing policy rollout?

irene: seeing large tail in router egress queues, p99 ~ 2.6s (baseline 200ms). p95 elevated too. logs show >40% of requests hitting a small subset of backends (hotspan).

maria: confirmed spike lines in ingress telemetry: ingress->router fanout skewed to zone-a nodes. weight table shows some nodes with 8x expected weight.

sam (oncall): @alex @jordan can you check change history on routing weights? we rolled policy v2.3 three hours ago.

alex: looking. rollout v2.3 did a shard affinity tweak at 13:02 UTC. diffs: changed seed mapping and enabled prefer-local for region affinity.

jordan: logs from router-r-14 show repeated remap events and a fallback loop to older model variants; see snippet:```[2026-03-15T13:34:08Z] remap start shard=r-14 -> node=zone-a-03``````[2026-03-15T13:34:09Z] remap fallback -> node=zone-b-07```. repeated handoffs causing KV cache thrashing.

irene: KV cache misses jumped from 5% to 64% on r-14, which will blow out latency for streaming (lots of long-lived contexts).

ops-bridge-bot: BRIDGE: https://meet.bridge.redwood/incident/1963123456 (oncall: sam).

sam (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) stop rollout (freeze v2.3) 2) force traffic away from hotspan nodes via temporary routing override 3) scale up warm pools for r-14 to reduce queuing. doing step 1 now.

maria: freezing rollout -> confirmed. API returns success for rollback.

alex: applying routing override: setting weight of zone-a-03/zone-a-04 -> 0.1 for 5m. command:```rctl set-weight --shard r-14 --node zone-a-03 --weight 0.1``` Applying.

jordan: after override p95 dropped from 1.2s -> 480ms, p99 trending down but still ~1.1s. streaming stall count halved.

irene: pushing cache warmers to r-14: starting 4 warmers to prefill KV slots. logs: "warmup: success 4/4".

sam (oncall): good. need to assess customer impact: which customers saw degraded streaming? get top-10 impacted apps.

alex: query run: top impacted tenants: corp-ai-bot, search-sim, docs-summarizer. Each reported >10% request errors/partial streams. notifying account success.

maria: note: metric anomaly shows region skew began ~12:58 UTC, a few minutes after preflight validation passed. suspect race in weight recompute under high fanout.

jordan: root cause hypothesis: policy v2.3 uses new hashing + prefer-local fallback which, combined with recent shard reshuffle, created a tiny hotspan. when remaps happened they cascaded and caused KV invalidation, leading to streaming stalls.

sam (oncall): next steps while we keep override: 1) revert policy v2.3 fully and redeploy v2.2 2) run a canary that simulates high-fanout to validate mapping 3) postmortem and follow-ups (hotspan detection alert + safer rollouts). executing revert now.

alex: revert started. redeploy v2.2 -> success on control plane. monitoring.

jordan: after revert p99 down to 350ms, p95 ~ 160ms. streaming errors near baseline.

irene: closing immediate mitigation: weights back to normal, KV miss rate down to 6%.

sam (oncall): great. documenting timeline for the postmortem. I'll keep bridge open for 30m for safety. assigned owners: rollback validation (alex), hotspan detector (maria), rollout gating (jordan).

maria: will add a temporary alert: if >30% of requests map to <5% of nodes -> page SRE.

ops-bridge-bot: UPDATE: incident status -> mitigated (SLOs recovered). oncall: sam.

sam (oncall): thanks all. I'll file the incident ticket with impact summary and customer list, and schedule postmortem review tomorrow. please add any logs or findings to the ticket: INC-1963123456. :thumbsup:
